hero.title: Mercedes-Benz OM613 Engine - Replacement Cost, Problems & Compatibility
hero.description: The OM613 is Mercedes-Benz’s 3.2-litre inline-5 common-rail diesel (CDI), bridging the gap between the older OM606 and the later OM642 in flagship models like the W211 E-Class and W220 S-Class. Reconditioned OM613 engines typically start from £2,800 , serving as a robust, torque-rich option for classic and high-mileage Mercedes restorations.

costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz OM613 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an OM613 engine typically takes 10-14 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the swirl flap system, injector seals, and turbocharger actuator. Because the OM613 is an early common-rail design, recon specialists often upgrade the swirl flap mechanism to a more reliable aftermarket unit or perform a verified delete, alongside replacing all injector seals as standard. failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM613 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Injector Seal Weeping ("Black Death") - All variants
items.whatHappens: The copper washer seals at the base of the injectors degrade, allowing high-pressure combustion gases to escape. This creates a black, crusty carbon buildup around the injector heads, leading to a distinct tapping noise, rough idling, and a strong smell of exhaust in the cabin.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a routine maintenance item, not a terminal failure. Replacing the seals and cleaning the cylinder head is inexpensive and should be done preventatively.

items.title: Swirl Flap Motor Failure - All variants
items.whatHappens: The plastic gears inside the electronic swirl flap motor strip over time, causing the ECU to throw a check engine light and default the engine to limp mode. In some cases, the flaps themselves can seize in the inlet manifold due to carbon buildup.
items.repairVsReplace: The actuator motor can be replaced independently and relatively cheaply. However, if the flaps are seized or the manifold is heavily carboned, a full inlet manifold replacement or verified delete is required.

items.title: Turbocharger Actuator Wear - High-mileage units
items.whatHappens: The wastegate actuator rod and linkage can corrode or seize, leading to inconsistent boost pressure, sluggish acceleration, and potential over-boosting if the flap sticks closed.
items.repairVsReplace: Actuator replacement is a straightforward and cost-effective repair. If the turbocharger internals have suffered damage from prolonged over-boosting, a full turbo rebuild or replacement is necessary.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM613 is generally more robust than the OM606 it replaced, featuring a stronger block and fewer timing chain issues. Units maintained with regular oil changes and timely injector seal replacements routinely exceed 250,000 miles without major internal issues .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-Benz OM613
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, just above the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. The OM613 is sometimes confused with the older 3.0L inline-6 OM606 or the later 3.2L V6 OM642. Fitting the wrong revision or assuming interchangeability matters significantly: the OM613 has a unique 5-cylinder firing order, specific engine mounts, and a distinct wiring loom and ECU mapping that will not function correctly in a 6-cylinder chassis.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM613 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM613 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented replacement of the swirl flap actuator and injector seals. Given the age of these vehicles, the primary risk is hidden carbon buildup or degraded rubber components, so a compression test is mandatory before purchase.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM613 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will address the common failure points by upgrading or replacing the swirl flap system, fitting new injector seals, and refreshing the turbo actuator, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM613 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage G-Class applications or classic W220 S-Class restorations where originality and maximum longevity are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM613 engine is installed by specialists familiar with early Mercedes CDI systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM613 is typically found in W211, W220, W463, and W215 vehicles valued between £4,000 and £15,000, a full replacement can represent a significant portion of the host's worth. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing .

items.question: How much does a Mercedes OM613 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes OM613 engine typically costs between £2,800 and £4,500 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £3,500 to £5,500 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £800 but carry higher risk due to the engine's age. items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM613 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are injector seal weeping ("Black Death"), swirl flap motor failure, and turbocharger actuator wear. Injector seal failure causes black carbon buildup and rough idling but is a cheap preventative fix, whereas swirl flap motor failure triggers limp mode and may require inlet manifold attention. Get quotes for a rebuilt OM613 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the OM613 engine?
items.answer: The OM613 was fitted to the W211 E-Class (E 320 CDI), the W220 S-Class (S 320 CDI), the W463 G-Class (G 320 CDI), and the W215 CL-Class (CL 320 CDI), serving as the premium inline-5 diesel for these flagship chassis between 2002 and 2005. items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned OM613 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned OM613 is strongly recommended over a used unit. A proper rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by upgrading or replacing the swirl flap system, fitting new injector seals, and refreshing the turbo actuator, whereas used engines often hide stretched components and carboned manifolds. Compare reconditioned OM613 engine prices from UK specialists

items.question: How do I know if my car has the OM613 and not the OM606 or OM642?
items.answer: The OM613 is a distinct 3.2L inline-5, producing a unique 5-cylinder rumble compared to the inline-6 OM606 or the V6 OM642. The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block above the oil filter housing and is also listed on your V5C logbook.
